name: DigiParser
summary: Document extraction for manufacturers that turns customer purchase orders and supplier invoices into structured fields and line items, with review before export, email-inbox processing, an API and integrations; priced by pages per month.
best_for: manufacturers and distributors that retype customer purchase orders or supplier invoices and want the fields and line items extracted for review, then sent to Sheets, Xero, an ERP via Zapier or Make, or their own system through the API
skip_if: your volume swings a lot from month to month, you need a refund route after paying, or you process receipts for bookkeeping, where a capture tool built for accountants fits better
honest_knock: Billing is per page, not per document, so multi-page POs and invoices use up the allowance faster than the plan names suggest, and confidence scoring doubles the credits per page. Unused credits expire every month, also on yearly plans, and a charged subscription is not refunded. AI splitting, classification and confidence scores start on Pro at $149 a month billed yearly. The ~99% accuracy, 2,000+ businesses and 5M+ documents on the home page are DigiParser's own figures.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month billed monthly for 500 pages a month, 5 parsers and 3 team members
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-22 in a headless browser in both billing views: every plan price below is unchanged. The page also runs a limited-time offer of 50% off the first month on any plan, and the comparison table lists one-time refill packs for extra pages.) (read 2026-10-13 in a live browser on digiparser.com/pricing in both the monthly and the yearly view, with the FAQ opened, and on the home page) Three self-serve plans, priced by pages processed per month, each with a 7-day free trial that needs no card. Starter is $69 a month billed monthly, or $49 a month billed yearly ($588 a year): 500 pages a month, 5 parsers and 3 team members, table and field extraction, email-inbox processing, API access and integrations. Pro is $199 monthly or $149 a month yearly ($1,788): 2,000 pages, 25 parsers, 10 team members, AI splitting of multi-invoice PDFs, document-type rules, classification, per-field confidence scores and custom roles. Scale is $399 monthly or $299 a month yearly ($3,588): 5,000 pages, 100 parsers, 25 team members, extraction modes and your own storage. Enterprise is custom for 10,000+ pages, with SSO, your own AI key, white label and on-premise options. EU and US hosting and a standard DPA come with every plan. The FAQ sets the rules: each page uses one credit, confidence scoring costs one more credit per page when enabled, unused credits do not roll over, yearly plans still hand out credits month by month, an upgrade mid-period is charged as a prorated difference, and once a subscription has been charged DigiParser does not issue refunds, though it asks you to contact support with a valid reason.

Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-22.

recent_change.text: DigiParser parsers can now use document type rules: either process only the document types you select, or skip the types you select, and everything else is handled the other way. The rules need the Pro plan or higher and cost 0.1 credit for each document checked, whether it is processed or skipped. Email intake also lets a parser accept mail only from listed addresses or domains and limit which attachment file types it takes.

compare_with.name: Dext
compare_with.why: Dext is in our dossiers too, re-verified on 10 October 2026: from $25.21 a month billed annually for 250 documents and 5 users ($31.50 billed monthly), excluding tax, with line-item extraction an add-on. DigiParser, read on 13 October 2026, starts at $49 a month billed yearly for 500 pages and 3 team members, with line items included. They aim at different desks: Dext captures receipts and bills for bookkeeping into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage and counts documents, while DigiParser turns POs and invoices into data for operations and counts pages.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested DigiParser on a trial account that we created. Onboarding took about 1 minute; a self-made, clean purchase order of 3 pages was read in under 30 seconds, with 0 of 11 fields and 0 of 30 line cells wrong, and the CSV export had 6 rows and 23 columns equal to the screen. The 3 pages cost 3 credits, so pages are what counts. One clean pdf is no evidence for the ~99% accuracy on the pricing page. The prices in the app and on the pricing page are the same as in our dossier, with a 50% first month banner on top. The checkout of Starter yearly showed US$588,00 per year with a choice of card or PayPal; nothing was filled in. Cancelling was not tried: a trial has no subscription, and the only removal route is Remove Team. Account and start: we created the account (EU region) and our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab of our browser, starting at 07:57:50 on 19 November 2026. The interface was already in English and no language setting was seen in the app. The dossier name is DigiParser and the review is on OSM (osm/digiparser-review.html); the dossier domain is digiparser.com and the app is the same product. The dossier says that we had not used DigiParser ourselves; this test is the first. Onboarding: 4 steps, Create document parser, What to extract, Upload document and View extracted data. Step 1: the name Test Purchase Orders and the type Purchase order. Step 2: the suggested fields Order Number, Order Date, Buyer Name, Buyer Address, Buyer Email, Supplier Name, Supplier Address, Supplier Email, Line Items, Currency and Total Amount, passed on unchanged with Continue. Step 3: Try your parser on one real document, or pick a sample below. Your trial includes up to 20 pages for this step. No connection (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier, Make) was asked for and no card. The onboarding was finished in about 1 minute. Core action: a self-made, neutral pdf of 3 pages with invented data (purchase order PO-2026-0417, a customer called Northwind Test Fabrication Ltd, 6 order lines, a total of 1082.00 EUR) was uploaded through Drop here or browse the files. Nothing of ours was uploaded. The system went straight to the inbox with Processing...; the document was created at 07:58:22 and showed Approved with all fields filled at 07:58:49 at the latest, so under 30 seconds from upload to the first result (the first check after 5 seconds still said Processing, the third check was ready). The tooltip said Your data is ready. We've extracted the fields from your first document. Result: Order Number PO-2026-0417, Order Date 2026-11-12, Buyer Name Northwind Test Fabrication Ltd (the pdf said Customer:), Buyer Address, Buyer Email, Currency EUR and Total Amount 1082 were all right. Supplier Name, Supplier Address and Supplier Email were EMPTY, which is right because they were not in the pdf. All 6 order lines had the right SKU, Description, Quantity, Unit Price and Total Price (for example BOLT-M8-50, Hex bolt M8 x 50mm, 500, 0.12, 60, and PLT-ST-3, 40, 8.75, 350). Wrong: 0 of 11 fields and 0 of 30 line cells. That is one clean pdf; it is no evidence for the ~99% accuracy on the pricing page, so we do not confirm that figure. Credits: 20 credits in the sidebar before the upload (Trial ends in 7 days) and 17 credits after it, so a pdf of 3 pages cost 3 credits and pages are what is counted. Export: Export Data opens a dialog with the formats XLSX, CSV, JSON and XML and the options All Fields, All Fields and Tables, All Fields and Tables (Flatten) and Table: Line Items. A CSV with All Fields and Tables (Flatten) was downloaded (4,6 KB): 6 rows, one per order line, and 23 columns (for example Order Number, Buyer Name, Currency, Total Amount, Line Items.SKU and Line Items.Unit Price). The values in the CSV were equal to the screen. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 19 Nov 2026 in the app (Team settings, Billing, Simple pricing, no surprises) and on the public pricing page digiparser.com/pricing. Monthly view in the app: Starter $69 (500 pages a month, 5 parsers, 3 team members), Pro $199 (2.000 pages, 25 parsers, 10 team members) and Scale $399 (5.000 pages, 100 parsers, 25 team members). Yearly view: Starter $49 a month (billed $588 yearly), Pro $149 (billed $1.788 yearly) and Scale $299 (billed $3.588 yearly); the public page shows the same yearly amounts. These are the amounts of the dossier, so the price did not change since 13 Oct 2026. A banner in the app offers 50% off the first month (Starter $34 for the first month, then $69 a month; Pro $99 and Scale $199 for the first month), applied automatically at checkout, with a countdown of 2 days 23 hours; the dossier does not mention it. Trial: 7 days, no credit card required, 20 credits (one credit a page; the onboarding says Your trial includes up to 20 pages for this step). Per-field confidence scores cost 1 page credit per page when enabled. AI splitting of multi-invoice PDFs is only on Pro and up. FAQ Do credits roll over?: No. Unused credits don't carry over. Checkout: Upgrade now on Starter (yearly) opened a Lemon Squeezy checkout for DigiParser Starter Yearly (500 credits/month) of US$588,00 per year, with the choice to pay by card or with PayPal. The checkout text was in Dutch. The test stopped there: nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. Without Upgrade the app asked for no card up to that point. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel on the trial; Team settings, Billing only shows the plans. The only route to remove things is Team settings, Advanced, Danger zone: Deleting the team will delete all resources and data associated with the team forever, with the button Remove Team. It was not clicked. Not tested: three separate pdf's, several invoices in one pdf and AI splitting (Pro and up), confidence scores, the integrations (Sheets, Xero, Zapier, Make and the API), the refund FAQ (not read), the difference between a monthly and a yearly invoice, mail to the inbox address of the parser, and entering the result in an ERP. Clean up: the account, the team, the parser Test Purchase Orders and the test document stay; the trial runs 7 days with 17 credits left; the CSV is kept outside the evidence folder; our own tab was closed and our other tabs were not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The trial gives 20 pages and every page counts, so the 3-page test already used 3 of 20 credits. Credits do not roll over. A banner with a countdown pushes 50% off the first month. The checkout text was in Dutch while the app was in English. There is no cancel button on a trial; the only route that removes anything is Remove Team under Advanced.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Three separate pdf's, several invoices in one pdf and AI splitting (Pro and up).
Messy, scanned or mixed documents, so the accuracy on real purchase orders.
Confidence scores.
The integrations (Sheets, Xero, Zapier, Make and the API) and mail to the inbox address of the parser.
Entering the result in an ERP.
The refund FAQ and the difference between a monthly and a yearly invoice.
Cancelling and removing the team.
